blocks.text: Surrey houses by price band, October 2026

113 houses sold in October against 1,033 listed. The price band with the most sales was $1,000,001 to $1,250,000, with 38 sold (34% of the month). Among bands with at least ten homes listed, the highest sales ratio was $900,001 to $1,000,000 at 27%.

blocks.text: Surrey Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Fraser River and Highway 1 north; Boundary Bay, 0 Avenue and the United States border south; Delta west, Langley east.
Six City communities: Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey, Whalley. City Centre is a planning core inside Whalley, not a board area.
Newton, on 72 Avenue and King George Boulevard, is the most populous town centre.

blocks.text: Surrey Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Fleetwood is primarily residential per the City; Whalley holds the emerging high rises — detached stock thins only at City Centre.
7491 144 Street: City report proposes RA (Acreage Residential) to R4/R5/R6 rezoning, nine lots — Newton's subdivide pattern.
Crescent Beach homes front Boundary Bay; Panorama Ridge holds ridge lots above the Nicomekl lowland.

blocks.text: Surrey Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Zoning: Surrey Zoning By-law, 1993, No. 12000. July 8, 2024: 20 single-family and duplex zones consolidated into nine small-scale zones.

Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH): over 72,000 lots under 4,050 square metres inside the urban containment boundary — suite, garden suite, coach house, duplex, houseplex, no rezoning where allowed.
One-third of Surrey is Official Community Plan (OCP) Agriculture, 95 percent Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) — A-1 lots carry ALR limits.
Crescent Beach Flood Construction Level (FCL): 3.30 metres Geodetic Survey of Canada (GSC); below it needs a Development Variance Permit (DVP).

blocks.text: Surrey Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Crescent Beach floodplain construction requires a geotechnical engineer; most Crescent Beach properties cannot connect to City storm sewer.
Metered billing: every four months; sewer at 88 percent of water supplied; 5 percent penalty after due date.
King George Boulevard Bus Rapid Transit (BRT): 30 percent designed, not fully funded — City update, October 20, 2025.
Serpentine dike raising: summer 2027. New pump station near 16000 block of 60 Avenue: late 2027.
Additional school tax applies to detached homes assessed at $3 million and over — City tax page.

blocks.text: Surrey Houses: development and new projects

items.t: 7491 144 Street, Newton — application 7920-0111-00, RA to R4/R5/R6, nine lots; status: variance report September 29, 2025 (as of November 3, 2026).

Surrey-Langley SkyTrain — 16 kilometres, King George Station to 203 Street, Langley City; Surrey stations Green Timbers, 152 Street, Fleetwood, Bakerview–166 Street, Hillcrest–184 Street, Clayton; status: under construction, July 2026 report (as of November 3, 2026).
Nicomekl dike rehabilitation — over 50 buildings protected near 48 Avenue and 184 Street; status: completion summer 2027 (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Surrey Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: 2026 residential (Class 1) total: $3.42731 per $1,000 — municipal $1.84251, other authorities $1.58480 (school $1.13480, TransLink $0.35860).
Class 1 parcel taxes, 2026: Capital $300.00; drainage $250.71; taxes due July 2.
Single-family flat utilities, 2026: water $1,195, sewer $1,661, total $2,856; waste $344.08.
Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT) applies — Province lists Surrey as a designated taxable area.

blocks.text: Surrey Houses: getting around

items.t: City Centre, Whalley: four Expo Line stations, ending at King George Station.
R1 King George Boulevard RapidBus: Newton Exchange to Guildford Exchange; every 10 minutes peak, 15 off-peak, 6 a.m.–midnight.
R6 Scott Road RapidBus: Scott Road Station to Newton Exchange via Scott Road and 72 Avenue.
Two United States border crossings in South Surrey per the City: Highway 99, Highway 15.

blocks.text: Surrey Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: City floodplain map first — Crescent Beach buyers unsure of the boundary are directed to the City Floodplain map and guide.
The permit page does not state an existing house's build level — verify slab versus 3.30 metres GSC.
Most river lowland is ALR farmland — confirm reserve status before assuming non-farm use.
SSMUH stops at 4,050 square metres and outside the urban containment boundary.

blocks.text: Jared's take on Surrey

Surrey is several markets under one name. There are tower condos in Whalley and City Centre, detached houses in Fleetwood, Newton and Panorama Ridge, and low-rise condos in South Surrey. My advice: shop the pocket, not the city.

faq.q: Can I add a coach house or houseplex?
faq.a: Often yes, without rezoning. The July 8, 2024 Zoning By-law No. 12000 changes permit Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing on over 72,000 lots under 4,050 square metres inside the urban containment boundary, including suites, coach houses, duplexes and houseplexes. Fit depends on zone, lot size and frequent bus stop status — check the lot.

faq.q: Is a low Bridgeview or Mud Bay house normal?
faq.a: No — it is a floodplain purchase. A City report maps Fraser River freshet to Bridgeview, Port Mann, Port Kells and South Westminster, tides to Crescent Beach, Mud Bay and Colebrook Road, and winter rain to the Serpentine, Nicomekl and Little Campbell lowlands. Bridgeview sits behind dikes. (check current — 2007 report)

No — it does not exist. The Ministry list for School District 36 (Surrey) records Tamanawis Secondary at 12600 66 Avenue and McLeod Road Traditional, Kindergarten to Grade 7, at 6325 142 Street. The district sets catchments — confirm the address in its school locator before a school-dependent offer.

faq.q: What does a legal suite cost yearly?
faq.a: For 2026 a secondary suite adds $454.00 water and $821.71 sewer, $1,275.71 total, plus $172.04 for garbage, recycling and organics collection each year. An owner who removed a suite must arrange an inspection, or the additional levy stays on the account for that tax year.
